solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Capital prison reportedly so regressive India emptied

indicators.note: reportedly says the slang word for jail is taken as it is heard, not as it is written

parts.note: nick is British slang for a prison or police station

indicators.note: regressive means the little word so goes backwards
emptied means India loses all its inside letters, leaving only its two ends

explanation.surface: A capital city's prison, said to be in decline, with India cleared out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' turns SO into OS; 'emptied' leaves IA from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus, an example of a capital.

clue.text: He seeks to impress citing famous paper, modern, unusual

definitions.text: He seeks to impress citing famous

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of the two words before it are put into an unusual new order

explanation.surface: A show-off quotes a celebrated, modern and unconventional newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who mentions famous acquaintances to impress others is exactly what this hyphenated term describes.

clue.text: Fruit firm repeatedly over barrel needing upturn

indicators.note: over places the doubled firm above the barrel in this down clue
repeatedly says the firm's abbreviation appears twice in a row

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: needing upturn says the barrel word is turned upside down, which in a down clue reads it backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: A fruit company keeps going back to a barrel that has to be turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing upturn' flips TUN to NUT, placed under COCO ('over').
explanation.definitionFit: The coconut is the large hard-shelled fruit of the coconut palm.

clue.text: Polished appearance of his: one he's adapted

indicators.note: adapted says the letters of his, one and he's are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone admires the smart look of a man's adapted belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam on well-buffed footwear is a polished look, so this term for buffed boots fits.

clue.text: Rise when supported by money

indicators.note: supported by puts the money beneath the first piece in this down clue

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a cent is a small coin, a piece of money

explanation.surface: Something goes up when there is money behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise and this word both mean a climb or upward movement; synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Normal English cut

parts.note: par means the normal or average level, as in 'below par'

explanation.surface: A standard English trim.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut away the skin of fruit is to trim it closely; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Vegetable regularly used prewar

indicators.note: regularly used means only every other letter of prewar is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A vegetable that was commonly eaten before the war.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea is a common green vegetable, an example of the class.

clue.text: At first reticent — is outgoing just after wine?

indicators.note: At first tells us to take the opening letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone shy at first turns sociable soon after a glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish red wine named after its region, an example of a wine.

clue.text: Dogma choice in part exaggeratedly male

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Picking a doctrine is partly an act of over-the-top masculinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes a showy, aggressive display of manliness; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Check a doctor is Polish

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A medic inspects a patient and pronounces him Polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is not the nationality here but the verb, to rub to a shine.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub something with soft leather to make it shine is to polish it; the leather lends its name to the verb.

clue.text: Country air — see loner transformed

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of air, see and loner are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Country air turns a recluse into a new person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierra Leone is a nation on the west coast of Africa, an example of a country.

clue.text: Teacher's sign of agreement on return

indicators.note: on return means the word for the gesture is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a nod of the head signals agreement

explanation.surface: A teacher's gesture of approval comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns NOD back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university lecturer or tutor, a kind of teacher.

clue.text: Association's nicest day out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of nicest and day are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A club's best day out.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of people or firms combined for a shared business purpose is an association.

clue.text: Caught by fine leg, Anthony, not very polished!

indicators.note: Caught by says the answer is held inside the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: A cricketer named Anthony is caught at fine leg, a clumsy bit of play.
explanation.walkthrough: FINE LEG is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace and refinement is a synonym for being unpolished.

clue.text: Be accepted — old boy thanks Home

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
ta is British informal for thanks
in means at home

explanation.surface: A former pupil is welcomed back, thanked and brought home.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses the rarer intransitive sense: a custom that obtains is one that is established.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs or rules that prevail or hold good are said to obtain; a formal sense meaning to be established.

clue.text: Sounds like fellow's water heater

indicators.note: Sounds like says the slang word for a man is heard, and its sound is written another way

parts.note: a geezer is British slang for a fellow, a man; the 's joins it to the definition

explanation.surface: A man's water heater.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a GEYSER is an old-fashioned gas water heater, not only a hot spring.
explanation.definitionFit: In British use the word names a gas appliance that heats running water, so a boiler for a sink or bath.

clue.text: It's a man's extraordinary staying power

indicators.note: extraordinary says the letters of the words before it are rearranged into something out of the ordinary

explanation.surface: It is a man's remarkable endurance being praised.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance or the ability to keep going is a direct synonym for this word.

clue.text: Describing straight path in drumlin earth

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the words that follow, crossing between them

explanation.surface: A geologist describes a straight route across the earth of a glacial hillock.
explanation.walkthrough: A drumlin is a long low hill shaped by a glacier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged along a straight line is said to be linear; an adjective describing a straight path.

clue.text: Extremely polite expert broadcast about conflict-free period

indicators.note: Extremely means take the two extremes, the first and last letters, of polite

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: about means the word for broadcast is turned round

parts.note: to emit is to send out or broadcast

explanation.surface: A very courteous specialist broadcasts about a time without war.
explanation.definitionFit: A time when a nation is not at war is a period free of conflict.

clue.text: Separate answer? Dad right!

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: A child asks for a different answer and Dad says it is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Being divided or kept away from one another is to be separate, an adverbial or adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Partner not finishing everything

indicators.note: not finishing means the partner word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an ally is a partner in a common cause

explanation.surface: A partner who doesn't see everything through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' drops the Y from ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole lot, every part, is a synonym for everything.

clue.text: Drink tips from Robespierre in style of the French?

indicators.note: tips from means take the letters at the two tips, the first and last, of Robespierre

parts.note: a la is French for in the style of
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A drink in honour of a French revolutionary, served in the French manner.
explanation.walkthrough: REAL ALE is traditional cask-conditioned British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional cask beer is a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Silvery grey tree

definitions.meaning: a pale silvery grey colour, like the residue of a fire
a deciduous tree with grey bark and winged seeds

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a pale grey colour and a common tree with pinnate leaves; two separate senses.

clue.text: In the morning I leave friend from Madrid

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, in the morning
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone departs in the morning to visit a pal in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Spanish word for a friend, so a friend from the Spanish capital.

clue.text: Posh headgear making comeback here in US?

parts.note: U means upper-class or posh, in British usage

indicators.note: making comeback says the headgear word goes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: A smart style of hat returning to fashion somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns HAT to TAH. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the American states, so a place in the USA.

clue.text: Gunners outline hectic competition

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
to trace is to outline or copy a drawing

explanation.surface: Artillerymen sketch out a frantic contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the frantic, competitive struggle of modern working life.
